# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

### 1. LOOP-DRAWING GAMES
*The primary task is to draw a single continuous closed loop*

#### 1.1 Unconstrained Path Loop
- **Slitherlink** — Loop drawn between dots; numbers indicate how many sides of a cell are used
- **Masyu** — Loop must pass through all circles; black/white circles impose turn/straight rules

#### 1.2 Cell-Traversal Loop
*Loop passes through cell centers*

##### 1.2.1 With Regional Constraints
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop passes through rooms once; must alternate between moon and sun rooms
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop must go straight or turn consistently within bold-line areas

##### 1.2.2 With Directional Constraints
- **Nagareru** — Loop direction constrained by wind arrows in black cells
- **Suraromu** — Loop must pass through all "Gates" in a specific order; starts/ends at numbered circle

##### 1.2.3 With Cell-Type Constraints
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells; arrow-numbers indicate black cell counts in a direction
- **Nurimisaki** — Loop-adjacent; white cells form promontories with specific connectivity rules
- **Mid-loop** — Black circles must be midpoints of straight loop segments

---

### 2. REGION/AREA DIVISION GAMES
*The primary task is to partition the grid into defined regions*

#### 2.1 Division into Rectangles/Squares
- **Shikaku** — Divide into rectangles; each contains exactly one number indicating its area
- **Choco Banana** — Black cells form rectangles/squares; white cells must not form rectangles/squares

#### 2.2 Division into Polyominoes
- **Fillomino** — Divide into blocks; each block filled with a number equal to its size; same-size blocks cannot touch
- **LITS** — Color one tetromino per bold-line region; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch; colored cells connected
- **Five Cells** — Divide into pentominoes; numbers indicate how many block-boundary lines surround a cell
- **Sashigane** — Divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends; arrows point toward bends

#### 2.3 Division into Paired/Symmetric Regions
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks each containing matching white and gray sub-areas of identical shape
- **Nuritwin** — Each bold-line region contains exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shaded cells connected

#### 2.4 Division with Evolving/Sequential Shapes
- **Evolomino** — Blocks grow sequentially along arrow paths, each adding one cell to the previous shape

---

### 3. CELL-COLORING / SHADING GAMES
*The primary task is to determine which cells to paint black or shade*

#### 3.1 Connectivity and Isolation Rules
- **Nurikabe** — Black cells form a connected wall; white cell groups each contain exactly one number indicating size; no 2×2 black squares
- **Heyawake** — Black cells cannot connect; white cells cannot span more than two rooms in a line
- **Hitori** — Eliminate duplicate numbers in rows/columns by blackening cells; black cells cannot touch; white cells stay connected

#### 3.2 Shape-Constrained Coloring
- **Choco Banana** — Black regions must be rectangular; white regions must not be rectangular
- **Shakashaka** — Place triangles in cells so remaining white areas always form rectangles/squares
- **Norinori** — Place dominoes (pairs of black cells) so each bold-line region contains exactly two black cells

#### 3.3 Number-Clue Coloring
- **Kurodoko** — Numbers indicate total visible white cells in four directions; black cells cannot touch
- **Kurotto** — Numbers in circles indicate sum of adjacent connected black cell groups
- **Usowan** — Numbers indicate adjacent black cells, but exactly one number per bold-line region is wrong
- **Tilepaint** — Entire tiles colored or not; diagonal-number clues count black cells in a row/column segment

#### 3.4 Gravity/Physics Coloring
- **Sto-stone** — Black cells in rooms; when "dropped" downward, must fill exactly the bottom half of the grid

#### 3.5 Maze-Creation Coloring
- **Nurimeizu** — Paint whole rooms to create walls; shortest path S→G must pass all circles and avoid triangles

---

### 4. NUMBER-PLACEMENT GAMES
*The primary task is to fill cells with numbers according to constraints*

#### 4.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness Constraints
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box without repetition
- **Hitori** — Remove duplicates from rows/columns by blackening cells *(also see Coloring)*

#### 4.2 Regional Number Sets
- **Ripple Effect** — Each room contains 1–N (N = room size); duplicates in a row/column must be separated by distance ≥ that number
- **Makaro** — Each room contains 1–N; arrow-black-cells indicate which neighbor holds the maximum value; same numbers in adjacent rooms cannot touch

#### 4.3 Block-Size Encoding
- **Fillomino** — Numbers define the size of the block they belong to *(also see Region Division)*
- **Chained Block** — Black cell blocks labeled with their size; blocks must form corner-touching chains; no two same-shaped blocks in one chain

#### 4.4 Crossword-Style Number Placement
- **Nansuke** — Fill grid with numbers from a given list, placed horizontally or vertically like a crossword

#### 4.5 Snake/Sequence Placement
- **Hebi** — Place snakes (sequences 1–5) in white cells; snakes cannot touch; directional visibility rules apply

---

### 5. CONNECTION / PATH GAMES
*The primary task is to connect elements or trace paths*

#### 5.1 Island Connection
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges (1–2 per pair); bridges cannot cross; all islands connected

#### 5.2 Pair Connection
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-branching lines that fill all cells

#### 5.3 Movement/Migration
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles horizontally/vertically into their home country; paths cannot cross; each country gets one circle
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles into gray areas; arrow paths cannot cross; gray area numbers must match sum of entering circles

---

### 6. SYMBOL/MARK PLACEMENT GAMES
*The primary task is to place specific symbols or marks in cells*

#### 6.1 Light/Illumination Placement
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs so every white cell is illuminated; bulbs cannot illuminate each other; numbered cells indicate adjacent bulb count

#### 6.2 Directional Mark Placement
- **Juosan** — Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers indicate the difference in counts; marks constrained in how far they extend perpendicular to their orientation

#### 6.3 Structured Shape Placement
- **Pencils** — Identify pencil shapes (straight strips with a tip); draw lines from tips through a number of cells equal to the pencil's number

---

### 7. HYBRID / MULTI-MECHANIC GAMES
*Games combining two or more primary mechanics in roughly equal measure*

| Game | Mechanic 1 | Mechanic 2 |
|---|---|---|
| **Nurimisaki** | Cell coloring | Connectivity/promontory rules |
| **Yajilin** | Loop drawing | Cell coloring (black cells) |
| **Dotchi-Loop** | Loop drawing | Regional consistency rules |
| **Sto-stone** | Cell coloring | Gravity/physics simulation |
| **Sashigane** | Region division | Directional arrow clues |
| **Evolomino** | Region division | Sequential shape growth |

---

## Secondary Classification Cross-Reference

### By Constraint Type

| Constraint Type | Games |
|---|---|
| **Adjacency / Touching rules** | Akari, Hebi, Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, LITS, Norinori, Nurikabe, Usowan, Yajilin |
| **Connectivity (all of type must connect)** | Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, LITS, Norinori, Nurikabe, Nuritwin, Nurimeizu |
| **No 2×2 same-color blocks** | Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin |
| **Directional/arrow clues** | Hebi, Makaro, Sashigane, Satogaeri, Yajilin, Yosenabe |
| **Shape matching / symmetry** | Chained Block, Double Choco, Evolomino, LITS, Nuritwin |
| **Single loop** | Dotchi-Loop, Masyu, Mid-loop, Moon-or-Sun, Nagareru, Slitherlink, Suraromu, Yajilin |
| **Gravity / simulation** | Sto-stone |
| **Ordered/sequential** | Evolomino, Hebi, Moon-or-Sun, Suraromu |

### By Solution Verification Method

| Verification Approach | Games |
|---|---|
| **Count-based clues** | Akari, Hashiwokakero, Heyawake, Juosan, Kurodoko, Kurotto, Shakashaka, Slitherlink, Usowan, Yajilin |
| **Size-based clues** | Chained Block, Fillomino, Five Cells, Nurikabe, Ripple Effect, Sashigane, Shikaku, Sto-stone |
| **Path/sequence validity** | Evolomino, Hebi, Nagareru, Numberlink, Satogaeri, Suraromu, Yosenabe |
| **Shape validity** | Choco Banana, Double Choco, LITS, Norinori, Nuritwin, Shakashaka |
